I've been looking at the compiler's error and warning output and noticed that the formatting of "Hint" sections is inconsistent.

*   When a compiler diagnostic message has both a non-empty body text and a hint, there must be a blank line (empty line) between the body text and the 'Hint:' line in the rendered output.

*   Hint text in operator-type-mismatch messages must begin with an uppercase letter: the phrasing must use 'The [operator] operator can be used with [type]s' (capital 'T'), not 'the [operator] operator can be used with [type]s' (lowercase 't').

*   Hint text must be line-wrapped to fit within the standard display width used by the rest of the compiler output; long hint strings that would exceed this width must wrap to the next line at a word boundary.

*   When two consecutive error blocks appear in a single diagnostic output, there must not be an extra blank line within the body of the first error block beyond what the message requires.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository to understand its structure and find the diagnostic rendering code.

Both edits are in place and `gleam-core` compiles cleanly. Here's what I changed, mapped to your four requirements:

**1. Blank line between body text and `Hint:`** — `compiler-core/src/diagnostic.rs`, `Diagnostic::write`. When a diagnostic has both non-empty `text` and a `hint` field, an empty line is now written before the `Hint:` line. (For operator mismatches the hint is baked into the body text and already had its separator, so this covers the `hint`-field path — e.g. the `MainFunctionIsPrivate`/`let_assert` style messages that previously printed `Hint:` immediately after the last body line.)

**2. Uppercase "The" in operator-type-mismatch hints** — `compiler-core/src/error.rs`, `hint_numeric_message`. Changed `"the {alt} operator..."` → `"The {alt} operator..."`.

**3. Line-wrapping of the operator hint** — same function now routes the message through the existing `wrap(...)` helper (the standard 75-column width used elsewhere in compiler output) instead of an unwrapped `format!`, so a long hint wraps at word boundaries.

**4. No extra blank line between two consecutive error blocks** — same function previously appended a trailing `\n` to the hint string. Combined with `writeln!` in `Diagnostic::write` and the per-diagnostic newline in `Error::pretty`, that produced a double blank line between stacked errors (e.g. the `multiple_bad_statement_*_fault_tolerance` cases). `wrap` returns no trailing newline, so the first block now ends with exactly the single separating blank line.

The final `hint_numeric_message` is a single expression handling requirements 2, 3, and 4 together:

```rust
fn hint_numeric_message(alt: &str, type_: &str) -> String {
    wrap(&format!("The {alt} operator can be used with {type_}s"))
}
```
